newsitem.title: GERMANY: Suspect confesses in German child-sex murder case.
newsitem.headline: Suspect confesses in German child-sex murder case.

text.p: A man in his 30s has confessed to the murder of a 10-year-old German girl whose body was found last Friday in woods outside Amsterdam, police in northwestern Germany said on Thursday.
A senior police officer, Hans-Juergen Bremer, said Kim Kerkow, who disappeared from her home town of Varel last Thursday, had been sexually abused before she died.
Bremer said the 34-year-old suspect told police on Wednesday he had taken the child to his flat in a village on the North Sea coast and killed her there.
He then drove the body over the border to the Netherlands and dumped it just outside the Dutch capital. The suspect, who was not named, was due to be remanded in custody on Thursday.
Bremer said the man had been arrested on Wednesday in his parents' home in the Wangerland district on the North Sea coast.

Investigators say the suspect had connections in Denmark and the Netherlands but they did not specify what kind. They said they were not ruling out the possibility he could have been involved in a international paedophile group.
Police say the suspect was convicted of manslaughter 18 years ago in a case that also showed evidence he had committed "sexual acts".

Regional authorities in northwestern Germany did not say if they saw any link between the murder of Kerkow and that of another 10-year-old girl, Ramona Krauss, whose corpse was found in Jena, eastern Germany on Wednesday.
Jena prosecutors said on Wednesday there could be a connection, and that a car similar to a black BMW seen in Varel before Kerkow disappeared had also been spotted in Jena.
Authorities in northwestern Germany said their suspect had been apprehended in a black Mazda.
The two cases have evoked memories for Germans of a child sex and murder scandal in Belgium last year.
At around the same time, a seven-year-old Bavarian schoolgirl was killed by a convicted sex felon who had recently been released from detention.
The case prompted calls for chemical castration of paedophiles, stiffer sentencing and an end to early releases for sex offenders.
